The paper defines a chiral Calderón-type surface operator to solve the direct electromagnetic scattering problem in chiral media.
The direct scattering problem involves a chiral dielectric with a perfectly conducting core.
The Drude–Born–Fedorov constitutive relations are used to model chiral media.
Electromagnetic fields in chiral media decompose into left circularly polarized (LCP) and right circularly polarized (RCP) components with different wavenumbers.
The scattered electric field satisfies a modified Silver–Müller radiation condition adapted for chiral media.
The Calderón-type operator is shown to be bounded, coercive, and compact in appropriate Sobolev spaces.
The existence and uniqueness of solutions to the direct scattering problem are proved using the Fredholm alternative.
The far-field operator is defined on the unit sphere and encodes the far-field scattering data.
The chiral far-field operator is normal and satisfies a key scattering relation involving its adjoint.
Injectivity and dense range of the far-field operator correspond to the absence of nontrivial electromagnetic eigenfunctions (chiral Herglotz functions).
The perfect conductor boundary condition requires the tangential electric field to vanish on the core boundary.
The variational formulation of the scattering problem uses sesquilinear forms involving the Calderón-type operator.
Vector spherical harmonics form a complete orthonormal system used to expand tangential fields on the spherical boundary.
The chirality parameter β is a positive real constant influencing wave propagation in the medium.
The factorization method of the chiral far-field operator is proposed for inverse scattering shape reconstruction.
The paper provides a rigorous mathematical framework for electromagnetic scattering in chiral media with penetrable and perfectly conducting components.
The Calderón-type operator acts between fractional Sobolev spaces of tangential fields on the scatterer's boundary.
The paper extends classical electromagnetic scattering theory to include chiral media effects and polarization coupling.
The far-field operator is constructed as a block operator matrix acting on a direct sum of subspaces corresponding to LCP and RCP components.
The study includes proofs of operator properties necessary for applying inverse scattering methods.
